context: Current closing price of Sempra (SRE): $93.63 USD as of 2026-07-14.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift across the three horizons, anchored around a current price level near 93.8. At the one-day horizon, the estimate stays very close to the present level because short-term price action in most financial instruments tends to mean-revert or drift only slightly, and without a specific catalyst in view, the most defensible forecast is near the last observed value. At the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate marginally higher to 94.2, reflecting a slight positive drift assumption — perhaps a mild trend or carry effect — while acknowledging that a week is long enough for meaningful price discovery. At the one-month horizon, the 95.0 estimate continues that gentle upward path, reflecting a longer-run drift assumption while incorporating more uncertainty about where fundamentals will settle over that timeframe.

The confidence interval widths widen substantially as the horizon extends, which is the standard consequence of volatility accumulating over time. At one day, the 90% interval of roughly 91.5 to 96.1 reflects typical daily volatility — tight enough that barring a surprise event, the price should stay within a few percent. At one week, the interval stretches to approximately 89.5 to 98.9, capturing the possibility of a meaningful directional move or a reversal from short-term noise. At one month, the interval of 85 to 105 acknowledges that over four weeks, macroeconomic data, policy decisions, sentiment shifts, and positioning changes can all compound to produce moves well beyond what any single-day range would suggest.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the downside, an unexpected policy tightening, a geopolitical shock, or a sharp deterioration in risk sentiment could drive prices well below 85 within a month. A liquidity event or correlated asset selloff could even push things outside the one-day interval on short notice. On the upside, a surprise dovish pivot, strong economic data, or a short-squeeze dynamic could propel prices above 105. These tail risks are real but assigned low probability — roughly 5% combined on each side — which is why they sit outside the 90% confidence band rather than inside it.

It is also worth acknowledging model uncertainty itself as a source of interval widening. The forecasts implicitly assume that recent volatility regimes persist and that no structural break occurs. If the underlying instrument enters a new volatility regime — say, due to a change in market microstructure, a regulatory shift, or a change in the correlation structure of related assets — then even the one-month interval could prove far too narrow. Forecasts at longer horizons carry an inherent epistemic humility, and anyone acting on them should treat the intervals as indicative
